public_rationale: The categorical prediction that agents will never work has a practical counterexample. Anthropic documents iterative agent execution, and Mozilla confirms repeated useful discoveries that led to shipped Firefox fixes. This supports usefulness in a bounded workflow with human oversight. It does not establish that general-purpose agents are dependable or that every advertised agent works.
limitations: The result depends on reading work as practical task usefulness, rather than universal or unsupervised reliability.
Humans configured the workflow, validated findings, and handled remediation.
The present-tense component is not separately resolved.

statement.excerpt: I’m tired of reading people talk about how we’re “in the era of agents” that don’t fucking work and will never fucking work.
statement.document_title: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that AI agents cannot become practically useful at carrying out their intended multistep tasks.
A bounded agent can work without being a universal worker. Human setup and review are compatible with useful autonomous execution of the intervening task.
A single selected demonstration is insufficient. Repeated useful results, verified outside the model developer, can contradict the categorical future claim.
The present-tense component concerns publication, but the supplied forecast classification makes the categorical never component the main adjudication target.
criteria.support_condition: No finite period of failures establishes that agents will never work. Supporting that categorical prediction would require a demonstrated general barrier that rules out useful future agent execution.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A deployed agent repeatedly performs useful multistep work, with its results independently verified by the organization using them.

evidence.locator: Section What's next for AI-enabled cybersecurity
evidence.explanation: Anthropic describes iterative tool use in discovering Firefox vulnerabilities, with human validation and Mozilla's involvement. This establishes an agent workflow rather than a one-response chatbot demonstration, although it is developer-reported evidence.

Mozilla confirms that its evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview produced many findings that were verified and fixed in a released browser. Together with the documented discovery workflow, this establishes repeated practical usefulness in a bounded task.

This study of production deployments identifies reliability and substantial human involvement as continuing constraints. It limits any broader conclusion about autonomous agents, but does not negate the verified security use case or establish permanent impossibility.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: Mozilla publicly confirmed that repeated findings from the model-driven security workflow resulted in fixes in a released product, satisfying the externally verified practical-use counterexample.
